item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday that the only way to remove the threat posed by Iran was to topple its government. “Iran wanted to destroy us; we stopped them. The lawmakers cited the LAUTECH Teaching Hospital in Oyo town, the Rashidi Ladoja Circular Road and the Ido-Eruwa Road among the projects whose timely completion, they argued, could deliver wider economic benefits to the state. They maintained that sustained investment in infrastructure would improve connectivity, create employment opportunities, stimulate commercial activities and ease the movement of people and goods across different parts of Oyo State. According to the arguments advanced during the debate, completing ongoing projects would also ensure that funds already committed to construction and other development initiatives translate into tangible benefits for residents rather than leaving projects unfinished despite substantial public expenditure. The lawmakers stressed that infrastructure development should be assessed not only by the amount of money committed but also by the practical benefits delivered to communities, businesses and users of public facilities. item.title: Otti to flag off Aba, Umuahia court complexes in November
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has announced plans to flag off the construction of ultra-modern court complexes in Aba and Umuahia in November. Each complex, according to the governor, will have an auditorium with a seating capacity of 1,000. Otti also announced plans to commission 15 additional court halls in phases, with 10 scheduled for commissioning after the current Legal Year programme and five before the end of the year. The remaining court hall is expected to be commissioned early next year. The governor made the announcements on Tuesday during the 2026/2027 Legal Year Thanksgiving Service held at the Queen Elizabeth Chapel, Federal Medical Centre, Umuahia. He said his administration was also working towards digitising processes across the executive, legislature and judiciary to improve efficiency and access to government services. Speaking on the theme of the Legal Year, “The Bar, the Bench and the Administration of Justice: Strengthening the Courts that Bind,” Otti stressed the need for cooperation among the three arms of government while preserving their constitutional independence. “The judiciary is a very important arm of government. There is no way the Executive or the legislature can work without the judiciary. But then, the lines are also very clear. And one thing you can be sure of with us is that we will always maintain those lines,” he said. The governor congratulated members of the Bar and Bench on the commencement of the new Legal Year and commended their commitment to due process and the rule of law. The Chief Judge of Abia State, Justice Lilian Abai, commended the working relationship between the executive and the judiciary, describing it as “a cord worth strengthening.” She disclosed that the state government had installed solar power systems at the High Courts in Umuahia and Aba. Abai also said Otti signed three laws on October 19: the Abia State Administration of Criminal Justice Law, 2026; the Abia State Restorative Justice Law No. 8 of 2026; and the Abia State Criminal Law No. 7 of 2026. She urged lawyers to protect the integrity of the judiciary and maintain a constructive relationship with the Bench. Earlier, the Anglican Bishop of Umuahia Diocese, Rt. Rev. Geoffrey Ibeabuchi, urged legal practitioners to discharge their duties with sincerity and accountability. He encouraged them to emulate King Solomon’s quest for wisdom and understanding, noting that members of the public relied on the legal profession for protection against oppression. item.title: 23-year-old Iranian woman sentenced to death over social media post
item.description: Iranian authorities sentenced a 23-year-old student to death for blasphemy in social media posts, rights groups said, as the judiciary’s use of capital punishment on political charges mounts. Najmeh Amini was arrested in February in the northeastern city of Mashhad and sentenced to death in September on charges of insulting the Prophet Mohammed, rights groups including the US-based Center for Human Rights in Iran (CHRI), Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) and the Norway-based Iran Human Rights (IHR) said in separate statements. Iran has already hanged 34 men on charges related to the January 2026 protests. But at least eight women, as well as Amini, are facing execution on political and security charges, according to rights groups. “I am an innocent girl. A young person with so many hopes and dreams. I have a mother and father who are waiting for me, a family who spend every night afraid of losing me until morning comes,” Amini said in an audio message from prison in September that was shared by the rights groups. “Remember my name. Perhaps I won’t be able to speak anymore. But as long as I am alive, I have one hope: that before the rope becomes the end of my life, I will see a free and liberated Iran.” The use of blasphemy charges, a capital crime in the Islamic republic, had been relatively rare in recent years. Bahar Ghandehari, director of advocacy at the CHRI, told AFP the “authorities may… be using this rare and severe verdict to make an example of her (Amini) and discourage similar acts as popular discontent continues to increase”. “Her case reflects the broader escalation of arbitrary arrests, politically motivated prosecutions, and death sentences following the bloody crackdown on protesters,” she added. – ‘Life at stake’ – “Amini’s life is at stake, and the international community must act urgently to stop her execution,” Ghandehari said. The verdict is not final and still subject to appeal. Details of her trial remain sparse, but according to reports in the regional daily Khorosan, Amini’s lawyer argued her posts were not intentional while Amini said she had been under the influence of hallucinogenic mushrooms she had consumed with friends. The precise nature of the posts was unclear. She was sentenced to death on charges of “sabb al-nabi”, the capital crime of insulting the Prophet Mohammed, according to the CHRI. item.content:encoded: Iranian authorities sentenced a 23-year-old student to death for blasphemy in social media posts, rights groups said, as the judiciary’s use of capital punishment on political charges mounts. Najmeh Amini was arrested in February in the northeastern city of Mashhad and sentenced to death in September on charges of insulting the Prophet Mohammed, rights groups including the US-based Center for Human Rights in Iran (CHRI), Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) and the Norway-based Iran Human Rights (IHR) said in separate statements. Iran has already hanged 34 men on charges related to the January 2026 protests. But at least eight women, as well as Amini, are facing execution on political and security charges, according to rights groups. “I am an innocent girl. A young person with so many hopes and dreams. I have a mother and father who are waiting for me, a family who spend every night afraid of losing me until morning comes,” Amini said in an audio message from prison in September that was shared by the rights groups. “Remember my name. Perhaps I won’t be able to speak anymore. But as long as I am alive, I have one hope: that before the rope becomes the end of my life, I will see a free and liberated Iran.” The use of blasphemy charges, a capital crime in the Islamic republic, had been relatively rare in recent years. Bahar Ghandehari, director of advocacy at the CHRI, told AFP the “authorities may… be using this rare and severe verdict to make an example of her (Amini) and discourage similar acts as popular discontent continues to increase”. “Her case reflects the broader escalation of arbitrary arrests, politically motivated prosecutions, and death sentences following the bloody crackdown on protesters,” she added. – ‘Life at stake’ – “Amini’s life is at stake, and the international community must act urgently to stop her execution,” Ghandehari said. item.title: 10 injured in Third Mainland Bridge crash, train collision averted
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni At least 10 passengers sustained injuries in a multiple-vehicle crash on the Third Mainland Bridge, Lagos, on Wednesday, while emergency responders averted a possible train collision at Ilupeju Bypass after a commercial bus broke down on a railway track. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) said the bridge accident occurred on Wednesday morning when a commercial bus stopped to repair a faulty tyre and was rammed by another bus. A trailer subsequently hit the second bus before fleeing the scene. According to the agency, emergency responders administered first aid to the injured passengers and evacuated them to hospital for treatment. The affected section of the bridge was later cleared and reopened to traffic. In a separate incident at Ilupeju Bypass, an emergency response team removed a broken-down commercial bus from a railway track with the aid of a light tow truck, averting a possible collision with an approaching train. The agency said emergency responders were on the ground to manage the situation. LASEMA urged motorists to avoid carrying out roadside repairs on highways and bridges, advising them to maintain their vehicles regularly to prevent accidents. It also urged residents requiring emergency assistance to call its emergency numbers, 767 or 112. item.title: Iran says Egypt entering Yemen war makes situation ‘more difficult’
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Wednesday that any interference in the Yemen war by Egypt or any other country would make the situation “more difficult”. “Egypt has sufficient experience to avoid entangling itself in such a highly complex conflict,” said Iran’s top diplomat in an interview with Iraqi state broadcaster Al-Iraqiya aired on Tuesday. “We believe that any foreign presence or interference will only make resolving this issue more difficult,” Araghchi noted. He added that Egypt has said it “will not enter Yemen or engage in a war against Yemen”. The decade-plus war between the Iran-backed Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government reignited in July. The Houthis seized much of Yemen’s Red Sea coastline in September and have since launched attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on state oil giant Aramco and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed on October 10. Egypt’s parliament on Monday delayed a debate on President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia until next week. Sisi had asked lawmakers to approve military support for Saudi Arabia if requested by the kingdom, which has come under near-daily attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis. item.title: Reforms Are Yielding Results, Okpebholo Urges Edo Residents To Back Tinubu’s Re-Election
item.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has appealed to residents of the state to support President Bola Tinubu’s administration, saying the federal government’s economic reforms are beginning to show in development and better governance. Okpebholo appealed on Wednesday when he visited the Ojuromi of Uromi, HRH Zaiki Anselm Aidenojie II, at the traditional ruler’s palace in Esan Northeast Local Government Area. He was accompanied by members of the All Progressives Congress (APC), according to a statement by Chief Press Secretary to Okpebholo, Dr. Patrick Ebojele. Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, speaking on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, when he visited the Ojuromi of Uromi, HRH Zaiki Anselm Aidenojie II, at the traditional ruler’s palace, in Esan Northeast Local Government Area. Speaking on his administration’s record, the governor listed road construction, the upgrade of primary healthcare centers, regular payment of salaries, and the building of schools among the areas where work is ongoing. He admitted that much of what his government is doing will not show results overnight. “Most of the work I am undertaking can not manifest in one day. It takes time because it involves construction,” he said. “Many roads have been completed, and we have started several others in different parts of the state. They will ease movement and improve economic activities in Edo,” he said. Governor Okpebholo also spoke about electricity, one of the state’s long-standing challenges. He said a 100-megawatt power plant is expected to come on stream in Edo South in the near future, with another project to add 16 megawatts. “These projects are part of our efforts to address the power problem in the state,” he said. The governor credited the federal government for progress so far. “The man driving that success is Mr. President. That is why I am here to tell you that I do not want Edo to be in opposition to this government because of the progress we are already making,” he said. Earlier, His Royal Highness (HRH) Aidenojie II, Ojuromi of Uromi,speaking on behalf of the Esan Enigies commended the governor for his efforts at fast tracking development to the state. He prayed for God’s blessings and prayed that God would continue to give him wisdom to pilot the affairs of the state. Aidenojie, who described the governor as his son, assured him that the anticipated eight years of his administration would be completed. item.title: Macron lands in Saudi Arabia on surprise ‘solidarity’ visit
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron landed in Riyadh where he is due to meet Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Wednesday, in a surprise “solidarity” visit after weeks of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Macron is the first Western leader to visit the kingdom since Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis intensified their attacks this month. The trip is part of a Gulf tour to secure diesel and petrol supplies as Macron seeks to bring down energy prices following violent protests in France sparked by rising living costs that have created a political crisis for the president. “The president of the republic is travelling to Saudi Arabia this afternoon to meet with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman,” a statement from Macron’s office said. The visit aimed to “demonstrate France’s solidarity with the kingdom in the face of the attacks carried out by the Houthis against its territory, and to continue efforts undertaken on securing and diversifying hydrocarbon supplies”, it added. In recent weeks, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have reached an unprecedented scale, forcing Riyadh airport to shut and the postponement of a major investment conference. A Houthi attempt to blockade Saudi ports is also hampering oil exports from the kingdom. AFP The post Macron lands in Saudi Arabia on surprise ‘solidarity’ visit appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NDC rejects C’River chairman’s listing in APC campaign council
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Cross River has rejected the listing of its state chairman, Goddie Akpama, in the purported All Progressives Congress (APC) State Campaign Council directory. The party made its position known in a statement by its State Publicity Secretary, Mr Cletus Amawu, and made available to Vanguard in Calabar on Wednesday. The NDC said an online directory had listed Akpama under the Chieftaincy Affairs category of the APC campaign council, describing the publication as misleading. It insisted that Akpama was neither a member of the APC nor affiliated with the party’s campaign council. The party also corrected the name displayed in the directory, saying his full and correct name was Goddie Archibong Akpama, not “Goddy Akpama”. According to the NDC, Akpama remains committed to his responsibilities as the party’s state chairman and continues to work towards advancing its political objectives. The party expressed concern that the listing could mislead the public, confuse political stakeholders, and undermine Akpama’s political standing. It urged those responsible for compiling, hosting, or circulating the directory to explain how his name was included, remove the listing, and issue a public clarification. The NDC also urged journalists, political stakeholders, and members of the public not to regard the listing as evidence of Akpama’s membership of the APC. The party said Akpama’s political activities remained within the NDC, adding that political disagreements should be resolved through legitimate engagement rather than the circulation of misleading information. It reiterated its demand for the immediate removal of the listing and a public clarification from those responsible. Amawu reaffirmed that Akpama remained focused on his political responsibilities under the NDC platform and would not be distracted by what the party described as attempts to misrepresent his political affiliation. item.title: How To Protect Yourself From Ebola Infection
item.description: The Federal Government on Tuesday confirmed the first case of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Ebola is a disease that spreads through direct contact with the blood or bodily fluids of an infected person or animal, according to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC). ﻿ Following the confirmation, below are facts on transmission/causes, symptoms, and how to protect yourself and loved ones. How Does It Spread? Ebola can be spread through: Direct contact with blood, sweat, saliva, vomit, or other bodily fluids of an infected, symptomatic person Touching contaminated surfaces such as clothing, bedding, or other materials contaminated with fluids from an infected individual Consuming infected wild animals, handling deceased bodies without safety gear. Know The Symptoms Symptoms typically appear two to 21 days after exposure. The symptoms include: Fever Vomitting Headache Diarrhea Weakness/Fatigue Bleeding Muscle pain Sore throat How To Protect Yourself Wash hands regularly with clean running water and soap, or use alcohol-based sanitiser. Avoid contact with dead bodies and wild animals. Ensure all meat products are handled hygienically and thoroughly cooked. Do not touch bodily fluids of sick individuals or handle deceased bodies without professional health protocols. Health workers should adhere strictly to Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) standards. Myth Vs Facts Let’s set the record straight! Myth: Ebola spreads via casual contact (handshake, hugging). Fact: Ebola does not spread through casual contact. It requires direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person. Myth: Ebola spreads through food and water. Fact: Ebola does not spread through food and water, but all foods should be thoroughly cooked. Drink clean water always. Myth: Ebola spreads through the air. Fact: Ebola is not an airborne virus. Transmission strictly requires direct physical contact with bodily fluids or contaminated objects from a person showing active symptoms. Myth: Healthcare facilities are not safe during outbreaks. Fact: Healthcare facilities are strengthening infection prevention and control measures, including triage systems, hand hygiene, use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), and isolation procedures to protect patients and healthcare workers. Stay informed and avoid panic. Spreading unverified rumours causes unnecessary fear and hampers response efforts. Always rely on official health updates. Oluyede’s recent sterling performance after his resolve to restore peace in the Northern region of the country earned him the laudable feat. At the well-attended conference that was held at the Army Command Officers’ Mess 1, located at Asokoro, Abuja, the organisers, under the aegis of Defence Correspondents Association of Nigeria (DECAN) explained that a lot successes under General Oluyede’s leadership have been documented. According to Odita Sunday, the leader of DECAN, an association of journalists covering defence and security issues in Nigeria, Gen. Oluyede’s leadership in ensuring jointness among the three services and his commitment to strengthening joint military operations is topnotch. The award to Oluyede highlights the importance of strategic military leadership, inter-service cooperation and constructive military-civilian engagement in advancing Nigeria’s security objectives. Here are some of the General Oluyede’s recorded successes that earned him a prestigious honour: Whole-of-government approach to national security Specifically, the award recognised his leadership in coordinating the operations of the Nigerian Army, Nigerian Navy and Nigerian Air Force towards addressing the country’s evolving security challenges. His leadership approach, according to the DECAN head, aligns with his military strategic philosophy of consolidating the capabilities of the Armed Forces of Nigeria through enhanced jointness, improved operational posture, personnel welfare and sound administration. Sunday said the philosophy also emphasises a whole-of-government approach to national security, recognising the importance of collaboration among the military, other security agencies and relevant government institutions. Under Oluyede’s leadership, enhanced cooperation among the services remains central to efforts to improve operational effectiveness and respond to complex threats across Nigeria’s security theatres. The CDS’ emphasis on jointness, seeks to promote coordinated planning, intelligence sharing and the effective deployment of military capabilities, rather than allowing individual services to operate in isolation. Troops’ better welfare and restoration of peace in North Similarly, the military chief has been matching his words with actions, where he has stressed the importance of personnel welfare and professional development in building a motivated and effective fighting force. The approach recognises that operational success depends not only on equipment and combat capability but also on the professionalism, morale and welfare of the personnel entrusted with defending the country. The CDS noted that contemporary conflicts increasingly required technological superiority, timely intelligence and effective management of the information environment, alongside conventional military operations. Several frontline troops, who spoke to Daily Trust had confirmed that their welfare has improved in recent times, and that their morale is very high to perform their constitutional duties. Against this background, the troops attached with different theatres of operations have continued to rescue kidnapped victims across 19 Northern States and some places in the Southern part of the country. Official data obtained from the Directorate of Defence Media Operations, being headed by Major-General Michael Onoja, revealed that at least 3,500 civilians were rescued between January and September 2026. Under the same period, no fewer than 1,773 terrorists disturbing some places in the Northeast, North West, North Central and a few other places in the South were neutralised while 569 terrorists surrendered after feeling the heat. Military deepens rescue operations in North as 27 victims freed in Katsina Neither relenting nor resting on its oars, troops of the Nigerian military attached with Joint Task Force North West, Operation FANSAN YAMMA, recorded another operational success with the rescue of 27 kidnapped victims and recovery of a motorcycle in Katsina State. Providing details on how the victims were rescued, Major-General Onoja explained that on 16th October, 2026, troops of Sector 1 received a distress call on terrorist activities in Gamji community, Sabuwa Local Government Area. According to him, the terrorists had abducted 27 residents, comprising 15 males and 12 females but troops responded swiftly and pursued the terrorists until they were rescued while some of the abductors were neutralised. “Troops responded swiftly, pursuing the terrorists along the Gangare–Kamba axis. On contact, troops engaged with superior firepower, forcing the terrorists to abandon their victims and flee in disarray,” he said. He stated that all 27 victims were rescued unharmed during exploitation of the area, adding that they have been profiled and handed over to community leaders for reunification with their families. In a separate operation on the same day, troops conducting a fighting patrol around Kurba village in Kankara Local Government Area encountered terrorists on three motorcycles. “The terrorists fled on sighting troops, abandoning one motorcycle,” the senior military officer added. He noted that the successful operations underscore the sustained offensive posture and operational effectiveness of troops of Operation FANSAN YAMMA in denying terrorists freedom of action and safeguarding vulnerable communities across the Joint Operations Area. General Oluyede, who commended the troops for their gallantry, assured residents of Katsina, Zamfara and adjoining states of the unwavering commitment to restoring lasting peace and security. 103 terrorists neutralized in 8 days Meanwhile, no fewer than 103 terrorists have been neutralised within eight days while their several logistics hubs and storage facilities in the North East were also destroyed. Specifically, the terrorists were neutralised between October 10 and 18, 2026 during coordinated airstrikes and intelligence-led operations by the air and ground troops attached with the Operation Hadin Kai. The military high command, while confirming the development, said the operations targeted Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters, leadership structures and logistics networks in Borno and Adamawa states. It said the air component recorded a major success on October 18, when it conducted a precision strike on the alternative residence of Abu Saleem, the ISWAP Wali of South Lake Chad, in the Arina Woje area of Monguno Local Government Area (LGA), Borno State. According to the Defence Headquarters (DHQ), the sustained air campaign involved seven strikes against terrorist targets during the period. The DHQ said intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance activities underpinned the operation, while subsequent human intelligence confirmed the killing of Jindullah, a prominent ISWAP fighter who reportedly served as Abu Saleem’s chief security guard. Military airstrikes bomb ISWAP security chief, Shura Council member In the meantime, the military also confirmed the killing of Jindullah, who was identified as ISWAP’s Chief Security Guard and Abul Kissa, a member of the group’s Shura Council, alongside other prominent fighters in an airstrike in the Lake Chad region. The strike, conducted under the Joint Task Force, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), also destroyed logistical assets, including boat engines and motorcycles believed to have been used by the terrorists for movement and operational activities. item.description: Delayed diagnosis and a dearth of essential medical resources continue to hinder Nigeria’s public health response more than the nature of the Ebola virus, a professor at the College of Medicine, University of Lagos, Dr. Alero Roberts, has said. ﻿ Roberts explained that the pathogen’s behaviour remains unchanged and predictable, adding that the real problem lies in systemic shortcomings and hesitation by members of the public, which she said compromises patient outcomes before medical intervention can begin. “I have no problem with the virus itself; the virus is doing what the virus does, it hasn’t changed its behaviour, and the virus is doing what the virus does,.” she said during an interview on Channel Television’s The Morning Brief on Wednesday, while reacting to Nigeria’s first confirmed case of the Bundibugyo strain of he virus. “We do have problems with the delayed diagnosis, seeking appropriate care and definitely with the availability of resources to cope.” The doctor also noted that no country in the world has the resources to manage the massive outbreak of the virus. “No country in the world today has the resources to cope with the massive outbreak of Ebola. Once the diagnosis has been made, Ebola becomes a nursing care issue, and there are just not enough nurses; kudos to the nurses, there are just not enough nurses to cope with the major outbreak of Ebola,” Roberts said. “Which is what we are seeing in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) already, so we must stick with prevention, border control, identifying, and as a public health physician I will be going with high index of suspicion to treat every patient as a possible case and initiate what we call the IPC ring. “The IPC ring is Infection Prevention and Control; we have got to initiate that because those are our first line of defense and they have proven very effective in the past,” she added. Speaking further on the breakfast show, Roberts said, “If you have been exposed but you do not have any symptoms, the good thing about Ebola is that you are not contagious.
